summary:
SELENARA is a lunar south-pole mission-planning platform designed to help explore and compare candidate lunar landing locations. It brings together astronomical calculations, solar illumination analysis, geometric Earth visibility, candidate-site comparison and mission reporting in one interactive application.

Using NASA lunar illumination data and astronomical calculations powered by Astronomy Engine, SELENARA allows users to investigate how location and mission time influence the planning context of five south-polar candidate sites.

The platform aims to make complex lunar exploration information easier to visualize, inspect and communicate while clearly identifying the limitations of simplified geometric models.
details:
SELENARA — Lunar Mission Intelligence Platform

Overview

SELENARA is an interactive lunar south-pole mission-planning platform developed in response to the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The lunar south pole presents unique exploration challenges due to extreme lighting conditions, permanently shadowed regions, crater topography and the changing geometric relationship between the lunar surface, Sun and Earth.

SELENARA brings several mission-planning perspectives together in one application to help users explore, inspect and compare candidate landing locations.

Key Features

1. Mission Dashboard

Provides an overview of the selected lunar landing site and relevant mission context.

2. Lunar South-Pole Explorer

Displays five candidate locations on a 2D south-polar stereographic map, with coordinate grids, site markers and selected-site information.

3. Solar Illumination Analysis

Calculates solar geometry for a selected location and mission date/time, helping users examine solar elevation, azimuth and illumination windows.

4. Earth Visibility Analysis

Evaluates the geometric position of Earth relative to the local lunar horizon for the selected location and time.

5. Candidate Landing Sites

Includes Shackleton Crater, de Gerlache Crater, Mons Malapert, Nobile Crater and Haworth Crater.

6. Site Comparison

Allows users to inspect candidate sites side by side using the platform's astronomical and location-related outputs.

7. Mission Reports

Provides a report-generation feature for communicating the selected mission context and analysis.

8. Methodology and References

Documents the astronomical models, data sources, assumptions and known limitations.

Scientific and Technical Approach

SELENARA uses Astronomy Engine for astronomical calculations and the IAU WGCCRE 2009 lunar orientation model. Candidate locations are represented using lunar latitude and longitude and visualized through a 2D south-polar stereographic projection.

NASA LROC Wide Angle Camera (WAC) South Pole Percentage Illumination data is incorporated as historical illumination context.

Scientific Limitations

The NASA WAC illumination layer represents historical observations from 2010–2011 and is not dynamically recalculated for the selected mission time.

Earth visibility represents simplified geometric line-of-sight visibility above the local horizon. It does not establish actual radio communication availability.

The platform does not claim terrain-aware RF simulation, detailed terrain obstruction analysis or mission-certified landing-site validation.

Intended Impact

SELENARA aims to make lunar south-pole exploration more accessible by bringing location, time, solar geometry, Earth visibility and candidate-site comparison into one navigable interface.

It provides an interactive starting point for understanding the factors that influence lunar landing-site exploration and mission planning.
